title: WHY SNOW LEOPARDS KEEP CHEWING
caption: From chewing bones to moving across rocky terrain: how snow leopards develop survival skills. 🐆 #SnowLeopard #Wildlife #AnimalFacts #WildVox Footage creators: MatthiasKabel; Ankur Panchbudhe; Fiver, der Hellseher; Squirrel83; Sanjay Khurana (video); Kevin MacLeod (original soundtrack removed). Original licenses: CC BY-SA 3.0, CC BY 2.0, CC BY-SA 4.0, CC BY 3.0. Edits: excerpts, narration, subtitles, portrait framing. Adapted footage CC BY-SA 4.0 where required; source/credit/license details: github.com/lulualcides-sys/wildvox-automation/blob/main/qa/credits/2026-10-29.md

narration_timeline.text: Why is this snow leopard working so hard on a single bone?
narration_timeline.scene: Real snow leopard gnawing a bone in captivity, no wild hunting claim.

narration_timeline.text: These big cats are built for gripping food, and their jaws do more than simply bite once.
narration_timeline.scene: Distinct captive snow leopard portraits in Sikkim and Leipzig; no invented mountain hunting.

narration_timeline.text: Watch how it clamps down, releases, then finds another angle.
narration_timeline.scene: Separate authentic snow leopard gnawing a bone.

narration_timeline.text: Strong jaw muscles and sharp teeth help tear food into pieces it can swallow.
narration_timeline.scene: Real snow leopard chewing and another adult portrait; verify low-resolution legacy source species visually before approval.

narration_timeline.text: In the wild, snow leopards also need careful movement through steep, rocky terrain.
narration_timeline.scene: Actual archival wild snow leopard walking on rocky Ladakh terrain at source seconds 20-25, not a 2026 sighting.

narration_timeline.text: Young cubs begin practicing the biting, gripping, and coordination that adulthood will demand.
narration_timeline.scene: Real cubs visible near the Salzburg Zoo rocky enclosure at the beginning of the authentic clip; no unsupported claim of a specific bite being shown.
